From a 2007 interview, Glen Hansard talks about a teacher who saw his love for music
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

In 2007, the late Glen Hansard visited The Current with his band, The Frames. During the interview portion of the studio session, Hansard shared a story about the teacher who helped inspire his career in music.

Hansard, the Irish singer who won an Oscar for the musical movie "Once" and the led the bands The Frames and The Swell Season, died on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, in a motorcycle crash in Dublin. He was 56 years old.

author: The Current
description:
A look inside Hawley Spin Depot, a record store in Hawley, Minnesota
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Nestled between Fargo and Detroit Lakes, Hawley Spin Depot is a place to spend time with music and with people. The shop specializes in both new and used vinyl alongside CDs, posters, and music-inspired décor, but what stands out is the range. “We’ve got a little bit of everything,” co-owner Mike Lemoine says. The stock is loaded with Americana, red dirt country, rock, dollar-bin curiosities, and rare pressings worth hundreds.

The space is cozy and thoughtfully constructed. Record bins made by family, walls lined with repurposed vinyl art, and a coffee pot that's always on. It feels less like a retail store and more like a friend’s house. There’s even a small setup for live sound — open mics, informal shows, or just a place to plug in and play.

Regulars return for the rhythm of new arrivals and word of mouth. When the town gathers — whet
title: Go inside Hawley Spin Depot, a record store in Hawley, Minnesota
